grammar.form: So + adjective + be + subject + that…; Such + be + subject + that…

exponents.text: Let me put that another way.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: So great was the change that I hardly knew the office.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: You have been away since March. Since March, we have written four reports.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: 'Since March, we have written.' The comma after the opening phrase. Good.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Now page one. What does 'access' mean here?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: By 'access' I mean a road that is open in every season.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Then write it on page one. A concept you do not delimit will be read as the reader pleases.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I put a note at the end.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Such was my own habit, and it cost me a year. Definitions come first.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The meaning is tacit here. Everyone in this building knows it.

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: And the ministry is not in this building. Make it plain on the page.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: So: 'In this report, access denotes a road open in every season.'

body.speaker: Mr Karimov
body.text: Now the rest of it can be argued about, which is all a report is for.
